title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 15° opens with the title 'Interprétation de Π_Q → N_σ^⇆' and summarises what has been done so far.

Setup, with my readings of the symbols:
- 𝓜 := 𝒩_{1,1}^{ét} is the arithmetic (étale) profinite fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q. It is an extension of Γ_Q by SL_2(Z)^∧.
- 𝓜^! is a subgroup of it attached to an extra symmetry, written ⇆. It is plausibly the group of the quotient of the Legendre (λ) line by the involution λ ↦ 1−λ, or of a similar 'level-2 with swap' structure. On the next page a section Γ_Q^{ét} ↪ 𝓜^! is written κ_{1/2}. This suggests a rational point of 𝓜^!'s stack fixed by that symmetry, plausibly λ = 1/2.
- The earlier (§11, eq. (217)) homomorphism goes from 𝓜 ⊃ 𝓜^! to groups M_{ρ,σ}^~ ⊃ M_{ρ,σ}^{~⇆}. Here ρ, σ are presumably the generators of the (oriented) cartographic / modular-type group with torsion relations.

This homomorphism was 'decomposed' into three pieces:
- (i) A trivial piece, 𝓜 → N_ρ^~ ≃ Ẑ^×, which factors through Π_Q^{ét} via a character χ (essentially cyclotomic).
- (ii) A 'geometric' piece (first display, numbered (325) here, but apparently (322) in the cross-references): 𝓜 → G_{ρ,σ} ≃ Ẑ^* ⋉ 𝔖^{+∧}, with restriction 𝓜^! → G_{ρ,σ}^⇆ ≃ Ẑ^* ⋉ M^∧ (cf. (218)).
- (iii) An 'arithmetic' piece (326): Π_Q^{ét} → N_σ^⇆ ≃ Ẑ^* ⋉ Ẑ (cf. (219)). This is an affine-type group, i.e. a cyclotomic character together with a Ẑ(1)-valued cocycle.

The page then recalls that the first homomorphism has been characterised arithmetico-geometrically (the word 'algébriques' is crossed out and replaced by 'arithmético-'). This was done in §13 for its restriction to the geometric part 𝒩_{1,1} ⊂ 𝒩_{1,1}^{ét}, after dividing by a finite central subgroup μ_? (μ_2 or μ_4, illegible). That gives
(327) M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}^~ := G_{ρ,σ}/μ_?,
and the characterisation goes through the tower of Fermat curves.

The next page completes the thought:
- One can say conversely that the hand-built ('à la force du poignet') homomorphism (327) 'describes' the Fermat tower.
- What remains is an arithmetico-geometric description of the induced Γ_Q → Ẑ^* ⋉ Ẑ.
- Using N_σ^⇆ ↪ G^⇆, this map is the composite of the section κ_{1/2}: Γ_Q ↪ 𝓜^! with the 'Fermat' homomorphism.

In modern terms, Grothendieck is studying a metabelian / 'Fermat-type' quotient of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} and of M_{1,1}. The geometric part is controlled by the Galois action on the Fermat curve tower x^n + y^n = 1, i.e. Jacobi-sum/Gauss-sum type data. He asks for an explicit arithmetic formula for the Galois character into Ẑ^* ⋉ Ẑ obtained by restricting along a rational (symmetric) base point. A natural guess is a pair (cyclotomic character, Kummer character of 2 or of a related number), but the page does not state this.
errors: Equation numbering is inconsistent. On this page the displays read (325)/(326), apparently overwritten from other numbers. The text then refers to 'le premier hom. (322)', and the next page cites (322) as 'Fermat' and (323) for Γ_Q → Ẑ^*·Ẑ, while (327) is numbered later. These are renumbering slips, not mathematical errors.
The finite group divided out in (327) is illegible (μ_a / μ_2 / μ_4). Which central subgroup is meant cannot be verified from this page alone.

ideas.what: Decomposition of the arithmetic π_1 of M_{1,1} (and of a symmetric sub-structure 𝓜^!) mapping to a quotient group built from ρ, σ into a cyclotomic part, a geometric part into Ẑ^*⋉(profinite cartographic-type group), and an arithmetic part Γ_Q → Ẑ^*⋉Ẑ.
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois action on quotients of π_1 of moduli stacks M_{0,3}, M_{1,1}; Galois representations into affine-type groups via tangential/rational base points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (general programme); this specific decomposition is unsure

ideas.what: Characterising the geometric homomorphism M_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ}/μ via the tower of Fermat curves; conversely, the hand-built homomorphism 'describes' the Fermat tower.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the Fermat tower / metabelian quotient of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}); Ihara's universal power series for Jacobi sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. Ihara (Annals 1986 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); G. Anderson (1989, hyperadelic gamma function); Coleman
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche manuscript sections; not in published works as far as I know

ideas.what: Use of a rational symmetric point (κ_{1/2}, plausibly Legendre λ=1/2) as a section Γ_Q ↪ 𝓜^!, and the problem of explicitly identifying the induced Γ_Q → Ẑ^*⋉Ẑ arithmetically.
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture-type splitting at rational points; Kummer-type cocycle attached to a rational point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (section conjecture, 1983 letter to Faltings); Kummer characters in Ihara/Deligne theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open an 'explicitation arithmético-géométrique' of the Galois homomorphism Γ_Q → N_σ^⇆ ≃ Ẑ^*⋉Ẑ obtained by restricting the Fermat-type representation along the symmetric rational section κ_{1/2}. Presumably the answer is a cyclotomic character twisted by a Kummer cocycle, but it is not determined here.
missed.quote: Il resterait maintenant à trouver une explicitation arithmético-géométrique de l'hom de Γ_Q ... dans Ẑ^*.Ẑ, induit par (325)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable computation in the Ihara/Anderson framework. A specialist could identify the Kummer character (e.g. of 2) and compare it with known evaluations of Ihara's power series at symmetric points.

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently links the Galois action on the profinite (metabelian-type) fundamental group of M_{0,3}/M_{1,1} with the tower of Fermat curves. This is the circle of ideas usually credited to Ihara (1986) and Anderson. The notes are undated but belong to the Longue Marche continuation, probably 1981–82.
missed.quote: dans la section 13°), via la tour des courbes de Fermat ... nous sommes arrivés à 'décrire' la tour des courbes de Fermat, via l'hom (327) construit ici 'à la force du poignet'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority/independence evidence: Grothendieck worked on the Fermat-tower description of a Galois quotient of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) in parallel with or before Ihara. Section 13° would be worth examining in detail.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a recap. It is notable as evidence that Grothendieck, in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation, tied the Galois action on modular/cartographic π_1 quotients to the Fermat curve tower (the Ihara–Anderson theme), and it states an explicit open problem. The details are too fragmentary to call a new result.
transcription_corrections: The display numbers on the page appear as (325)/(326) written over other digits (the transcription has '(325)' and '(326)'). The text below refers to '(322)', consistent with the next page's references to (322)/(323).
The superscript on 𝓜 is 'déf' (=def), and 'cf (217) (p. 69?)' — the page number is likely 69 or 695.
The superscript of N_σ in (326) is unclear; it reads like '⇆abs' or '⇆ab', not certain.
'mod μ_a' — the subscript is illegible, possibly μ_2 or μ_4.
The crossed-out start of (327) appears to be an abandoned symbol (possibly 'M_{0,3}'), now replaced by 'M_{0,3} — G_{ρ,σ}^~ := G_{ρ,σ}/μ_?'.
